newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Equatorial gets copper mine options.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Equatorial gets copper mine options.

text.p: Equatorial Mining NL said on Monday it had reached an agreement with Cyprus Climax Metals Co of the U.S. for an option to acquire two Cyprus Climax copper properties in Arizona and Nevada.
The options cover the Mineral Park copper mine near Kingman, Arizona, and the Tonopah copper ore body near Tonopah, Nevada.
The operation at Mineral Park is a dump leach, solvent extraction, electrowinning facility, producing between five and six million pounds of copper cathode a year, Equatorial said.

Preliminary investigations by Equatorial indicate that with modifications annual output could be doubled to between 10 and 12 million pounds of copper a year, resulting in cash costs falling below US$0.60 a pound and mine life falling to six years, it said.
The Tonopah property has the potential to produce about 40 million pounds of copper a year for 10 years at a cash cost below US$0.10 a pound, Equatorial said.
Upon exercising of the option, dated June 28, 1997, Cyprus is to be issued new shares equivalent to 4.5 percent of the then current issued capital of Equitorial, the company said.
After the recovery of development costs for Tonopah, Equitorial said it is to pay Cyprus Climax a sliding scale royalty of between US$0.02 and US$0.06 per pound of copper.
The royalty, commencing at US$0.02 a pound at a copper price of US$0.90 a pound, will rise to US$0.06 a pound at a copper price of US$1.20 a pound or greater, Equatorial said.

Equatorial said it intends to seek a North American stock exchange listing to access North American capital markets and to proceed to bring the Tonopah property to production , probably before the end of 1998, it said.

Acquisition of the the two properties, coupled with development of Equatorial's Tesoro joint venture copper project in Chile will take the company closer to its objective of achieving production of 50,000 tonnes of copper a year within five years, Equatorial's chairman, Stephen Gerlach, said in a statement.
"We now need a gold project to give us production of 50,000 ounces per annum and we are actively progressing such a project," he said.
